title: The Award Show Era
theme: Grammy wins, Soul Train Awards, and the recognition that defined 90s R&B
narrativePurpose: Test whether players know not just the music but the moment it was validated — who won, what category, what year, and who should have won instead
toneProgression: Famous wins everyone knows → category knowledge and undercard winners → inaugural categories and award show founding history

vault.note: Digit 4 (index 3) is always visible. Vault code 1-9-9-9 — the 41st Grammy ceremony, where Lauryn Hill swept five awards in a single night — the largest haul in Grammy history at the time. The night R&B and the Grammys finally occupied the same sentence.

rounds.name: RADIO HITS
rounds.description: The wins everyone remembers. The speeches people still talk about. The moments that defined what R&B meant to the mainstream.

questions.question: Lauryn Hill won how many Grammy Awards at the 1999 ceremony for 'The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill'?

metadata.fact: Lauryn Hill's five Grammys at the 1999 ceremony set a record for the most won by a female artist in a single night — a record that stood for years.
metadata.storyHook: Five statues. One night. The most dominant Grammy performance by a female artist in the history of the ceremony.

questions.question: TLC won Grammy Best R&B Album for 'CrazySexyCool' at which numbered Grammy ceremony?

metadata.fact: TLC won Best R&B Album at the 38th Grammy Awards in 1996 for CrazySexyCool — one of four Grammy nominations the album received.
metadata.storyHook: The album that defined 1994 got its official recognition two years later. The Grammys were late, as usual.

sources.title: TLC won 2 GRAMMYs for CrazySexyCool – Instagram

questions.question: Whitney Houston's 'I Will Always Love You' won which Grammy category at the 1994 ceremony?

metadata.fact: 'I Will Always Love You' won Record of the Year at the 36th Grammy Awards in 1994 — the category recognizes the performance and production of a specific recording, not the composition.
metadata.storyHook: The biggest song in the world at the time walking away with the biggest Grammy category. No surprises that night.

questions.question: Which Boyz II Men single earned the Grammy for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group at the 1995 ceremony?

metadata.fact: 'I'll Make Love to You' won Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group at the 37th Grammy Awards in 1995 — Boyz II Men won the same category the year before for 'End of the Road.'
metadata.storyHook: Back-to-back wins in the same category. Nobody in the 90s owned the Grammy stage the way Boyz II Men did.

sources.title: I'll Make Love to You – Wikipedia

questions.question: Brandy and Monica won Grammy Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group at the 1999 ceremony for which single?

metadata.fact: 'The Boy Is Mine' won Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group at the 41st Grammy Awards in 1999 — the same ceremony dominated by Lauryn Hill.
metadata.storyHook: The biggest rivalry in late-90s R&B walked away with a Grammy together. Life is full of surprises.

questions.question: Soul Train — which inspired the Soul Train Music Awards — was created and hosted by which television pioneer?

metadata.fact: Don Cornelius created Soul Train in 1970 as a local Chicago broadcast before syndicating it nationally in 1971 — the show ran for 35 years and became the primary television platform for Black music.
metadata.storyHook: No Soul Train, no Soul Train Awards, no Grammy category for R&B. Don Cornelius built the infrastructure that made all of it possible.

questions.question: The Grammy ceremony where Lauryn Hill won five awards was held in which year?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 1 OF 3 — YEAR OF LAURYN HILL'S FIVE-GRAMMY SWEEP

metadata.fact: The 41st Grammy Awards were held February 24, 1999 — Lauryn Hill's five-award sweep that night remains one of the most dominant individual performances in Grammy history.
metadata.storyHook: The year everything shifted. The Grammys finally caught up with what the streets already knew.

rounds.name: DEEP CUTS
rounds.description: Category knowledge. Undercard winners. The Grammy and Soul Train Award history that casual fans never tracked.

questions.question: Erykah Badu won Grammy Best Female R&B Vocal Performance at the 1998 ceremony for which debut single?

metadata.fact: Erykah Badu won Best Female R&B Vocal Performance at the 40th Grammy Awards in 1998 for 'On & On' — her debut single and the record that introduced neo-soul to a mainstream Grammy audience.
metadata.storyHook: The Grammy that told the industry neo-soul had arrived — and Erykah Badu was its face.

questions.question: At the 1999 Grammys where Lauryn Hill swept, Best Rap Solo Performance went to which artist for 'My Name Is'?

metadata.fact: 'My Name Is' won Best Rap Solo Performance at the 41st Grammy Awards in 1999 — Eminem's first Grammy win, announced the same night Lauryn Hill took five.
metadata.storyHook: While Lauryn Hill was rewriting Grammy history, a new face won rap's biggest individual award across the hall.

questions.question: Which R&B group won the American Music Award for Favorite Soul/R&B Band/Duo/Group for three consecutive years from 1993 to 1995?

metadata.fact: Boyz II Men won the AMA for Favorite Soul/R&B Band/Duo/Group three consecutive years from 1993 to 1995 — their commercial dominance of the early 90s reflected in the fan-voted format of the AMAs.
metadata.storyHook: Three years running. The most consistently rewarded group in early 90s R&B, and it wasn't close.

questions.question: Toni Braxton won Grammy Best R&B Album at the 1997 ceremony for which album?

metadata.fact: Secrets won Grammy Best R&B Album at the 39th Grammy Awards in 1997 — Toni Braxton had previously won the same category for her self-titled debut at the 37th ceremony in 1995.
metadata.storyHook: Two Best R&B Album Grammys in three years. Toni Braxton owned the mid-90s R&B Grammy landscape.

questions.question: The Grammy for Best Rap Solo Performance in 1996 went to which rapper for 'Gangsta's Paradise'?

metadata.fact: Coolio's 'Gangsta's Paradise' — from the Dangerous Minds soundtrack — won Best Rap Solo Performance at the 38th Grammy Awards in 1996, beating Tupac Shakur's 'Dear Mama' in the same category.
metadata.storyHook: The Grammy that the internet still argues about — Coolio over Tupac. One of the most contested wins of the decade.

questions.question: The Soul Train Music Awards first aired on television in which year?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 2 OF 3 — YEAR THE SOUL TRAIN AWARDS FIRST AIRED

metadata.fact: The Soul Train Music Awards first aired in 1987 — established as a counterpart to the Grammys, specifically designed to recognize Black music on its own terms.
metadata.storyHook: Don Cornelius built the show because the Grammys weren't doing the job. He was right.

rounds.name: HIDDEN GEMS
rounds.description: Inaugural categories. Buried wins. The founding history of the ceremonies that shaped how 90s R&B was judged.

questions.question: Mary J. Blige won Grammy Best Contemporary R&B Album at the 2000 ceremony — the first year the category existed. Which album earned her that inaugural award?

metadata.fact: Mary J. Blige's self-titled 1999 album 'Mary' won the inaugural Grammy for Best Contemporary R&B Album at the 42nd ceremony in 2000 — the first time the Recording Academy separated contemporary and traditional R&B.
metadata.storyHook: The first winner of a brand new Grammy category. Mary J. Blige made history twice with the same record.

questions.question: Soul Train began as a local Chicago broadcast in 1970 before going national in syndication in which year?

metadata.fact: Soul Train went to national syndication on October 2, 1971 — its first nationally broadcast episode aired in seven cities simultaneously, making it the first nationally syndicated Black-oriented music television show.
metadata.storyHook: One local show. Seven cities. The beginning of 35 years of Black music on television.

questions.question: The Grammy Awards were first presented in which year?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 3 OF 3 — YEAR THE GRAMMYS WERE FIRST PRESENTED

metadata.fact: The first Grammy Awards ceremony was held May 4, 1959 at the Beverly Hilton Hotel in Beverly Hills — 28 awards were given that night, honoring recordings from 1958.
metadata.storyHook: The ceremony that would eventually hand Lauryn Hill five awards in one night started with 28 total in a hotel ballroom in Beverly Hills.
